overview: Program-level QI project using the Model for Improvement: eight weekly baseline points rated from August and September 2026 forms, then three PDSA cycles from October 2026 to March 2027, with a weekly run chart of actionable comments.
population: All mini clinical evaluation exercise and case-based discussion forms completed for the 90 residents; each week 25 comments are sampled by form number from the week's completed forms.
exposure: Cycle 1 (October to December): feedback field relabelled 'What did the resident do well, and what should they do differently next time?' plus 20-minute micro-teaching in October and November. Cycle 2 (January to February): two separate fields, 'one thing to keep doing' and 'one thing to do differently next time'. Cycle 3 (February to March): a monthly one-page report to each faculty member with a sample of their own rated comments and the program median.
procedures: An administrator extracts comment text without dates, form layout or names and mixes baseline and current comments in each rating batch. Chief residents rate each comment against the three criteria using written definitions and examples; 20 percent are rated by both. Cycle decisions are made at the monthly faculty meeting from the run chart.

outcomes.name: Actionable comments
outcomes.measure: Weekly proportion of 25 sampled comments meeting all three criteria: specific behaviour, gap, concrete next step
outcomes.timing: Weekly; 8 baseline and about 24 intervention weeks
outcomes.why: Directly measures the feedback residents can use.

outcomes.name: Actionable comments by resident gender
outcomes.measure: Monthly proportion meeting all three criteria for women and for men residents
outcomes.why: Checks that improvement reaches women residents (claim c4).

outcomes.name: Faculty reach of the change package
outcomes.measure: Proportion of faculty attending micro-teaching and opening monthly reports
outcomes.why: Separates a weak idea from weak delivery.

outcomes.name: Forms completed per week
outcomes.why: Longer prompts must not reduce the number of assessments.

outcomes.name: Days from encounter to form completion

feasibility: Twenty-five comments at about 40 seconds each plus double rating take under 30 minutes a week, within the chief residents' two hours; relabelling is possible now and the second field from January.
biasMitigation: Comment text rated without dates, layout or names, in mixed batches
Written operational definition with examples fixed before baseline
Twenty percent double rating with monthly agreement checks
Run chart annotated with policy or rotation changes

biasFlags.label: Rater expectation
biasFlags.note: Two-prompt comments may be recognisable from their structure; double rating limits drift.

biasFlags.label: Secular change
biasFlags.note: Other education changes are annotated on the chart.

biasFlags.label: Sampling
biasFlags.note: Form-number sampling rather than rater choice.

flags: One outcome measure, one equity breakdown, one process and two balancing measures
parsimony.simplestPath: One weekly measure on a run chart, three cycles, existing forms and meetings.

theoreticalFramework: Model for Improvement; audit and feedback principles for the individual reports.
summary: Three PDSA cycles after eight baseline weeks with one outcome measure, a gender breakdown and two balancing measures.
